A grammar chapter on the little words that place things in space — *on, under, next to, in, from* — and one tricky pair, **لـ (le)** versus **ليه (leeh)**. Tap any example to reveal its franco and English.

## Place words

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| فوق - fo2 | on / above |
| تحت - ta7t | under / below |
| جنب - ganb | next to / beside |
| قدام - 2oddam | in front of |
| ورا - wara | behind |
| بين - bein | between |
| جوه - gowwa | inside |
| بره - barra | outside |
| على - 3ala | on / onto |
| في - fi | in / at |

## "X is [somewhere] Y"

Because there's no verb "to be" (the *Pronouns* chapter), saying where something is takes no verb at all. Just line up **[thing] + [place word] + [the place]**:

<details class="frase">
<summary>الكتاب فوق الترابيزة</summary>
<span class="fr">el-ketab fo2 el-tarabeza</span>
<span class="en">the book is on the table</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>القلم تحت الكرسي</summary>
<span class="fr">el-2alam ta7t el-korsi</span>
<span class="en">the pen is under the chair</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا جنب الباب</summary>
<span class="fr">ana ganb el-bab</span>
<span class="en">I'm next to the door</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>القطة جوه الصندوق</summary>
<span class="fr">el-2otta gowwa el-sondo2</span>
<span class="en">the cat is inside the box</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>الكلب بره البيت</summary>
<span class="fr">el-kalb barra el-bet</span>
<span class="en">the dog is outside the house</span>
</details>

## في and من — "in / at" and "from"

These two carry most of your location work.

- **في (fi)** = in / at: *ana fi el-bet* "I'm at home", *bashta8al fi maktab* "I work in an office".
- **من (men)** = from: *ana men masr* "I'm from Egypt".

A note worth keeping: with a verb of motion you often need **no preposition at all** for the destination — *baroo7 el-sho8l* is simply "I go (to) work", with no word for "to".

## لـ and ليه — a pair to keep apart

They look almost the same but do completely different jobs:

- **لـ (le)** = to / for / until — *el-hedeyya le Mona* "the gift is for Mona", *men el-sa3a talata le el-5amsa* "from three to five".
- **ليه (leeh)** = **why** — a question word: *betet3allim 3araby leeh?* "why are you learning Arabic?".

One is a little preposition glued to the next word; the other is a full question word that lands at the end of the sentence.

## Examples

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا من البرازيل</summary>
<span class="fr">ana men el-Brazil</span>
<span class="en">I'm from Brazil</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>بشتغل في مكتب</summary>
<span class="fr">bashta8al fi maktab</span>
<span class="en">I work in an office</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>الرسالة لكريم</summary>
<span class="fr">el-resala le Karim</span>
<span class="en">the letter is for Karim</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>بتتعلم عربي ليه؟</summary>
<span class="fr">betet3allim 3araby leeh?</span>
<span class="en">why are you learning Arabic?</span>
</details>

## Vocabulary

| Arabic - franco | English |
|---|---|
| ترابيزة - tarabeza | table |
| كرسي - korsi | chair |
| باب - bab | door |
| صندوق - sondo2 | box |
| هدية - hedeyya | gift |

**1.** The book is on the table.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>

<span class="fr">el-ketab fo2 el-tarabeza</span>
</details>

**2.** The cat is under the chair.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">القطة تحت الكرسي</span>
<span class="fr">el-2otta ta7t el-korsi</span>
</details>

**3.** I'm next to the door.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">أنا جنب الباب</span>
<span class="fr">ana ganb el-bab</span>
</details>

### Exercise 3 — في / من / لـ / ليه

**1.** I'm from Egypt.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">أنا من مصر</span>
<span class="fr">ana men masr</span>
</details>

**2.** Why?

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">ليه؟</span>
<span class="fr">leeh?</span>
</details>

**3.** The letter is for Karim.

<details class="ans">
<summary>Show answer</summary>
<span class="ar">الرسالة لكريم</span>
<span class="fr">el-resala le Karim</span>
</details>
